ov: A tree-dwelling relative of raccoons and coatis from the rainforests of Mexico and Central and South America. It is strictly nocturnal, has a long prehensile tail, and eats mostly ripe fruit, especially figs. It is also called the honey bear.
rg: Tropical rainforests of Mexico, Central America and South America.
df: About 90% fruit, mostly figs, plus leaves, flowers, nectar and sometimes ants.
fx: Its slender 13 cm tongue scoops fruit pulp and licks nectar from flowers, so it may help pollinate them.
Kinkajous may live up to 40 years in captivity.
notes: The animals.js fact is confirmed (13 cm tongue, prehensile tail).
